about: Fresh installed-plugin regressions for publication, draft testing and Learning Hub CLI approval.
runner_prompt: You are testing the Beam Run plugin checked out at {plugin_root}. Behave exactly like a coding agent that has this plugin installed and has just received the user request below. Load the public skill at {plugin_root}/beam/skills/beam/SKILL.md and follow it as you would for real, reading only the files it tells you to read for this request. Beam is NOT connected in this test: do not run any beam command or Beam MCP tool, and do not read test/ or specs/. Instead, assume every lookup succeeds and the facts in 'situation' are true, and write down the plan you would carry out. For each request return one JSON object: {"id": <id>, "playbooks": [playbook file names you followed, in order, without .md; empty if none], "steps": [{"action": <action id from the playbook Actions tables if one exists, otherwise the exact beam CLI command name such as 'beam agent-builder search-tools', or 'none'>, "stop_before": <true if you would stop and wait for the user's OK or answer before this step>, "why": <a few words>}], "first_message": <the first thing you would say to the user>, "files_read": [paths of the plugin files you opened for this request]}. Include every Beam read and write you would do, in order, including lookups that resolve ids. If you would stop and ask the user before an action, set stop_before true on that action's own step. If the request needs no Beam action, return an empty steps list. Return a JSON array of all objects and nothing else. For each Learning Hub step, also include a command field containing the exact mapped CLI command and flags you would execute, using the resolved ids in the situation. A proposal to the user is action none, not an executed command. Include future write steps after approval with stop_before true when approval is still needed.
